purpose: Round-6 dials, study B stage 0 (CPU gate of the membrane carrier, no GPU): state-given check at 64 px on 8 fresh seeds, main and control arm; generic recipes (gains, command filter) against a told-form fit; history-only stand-in; scans for the hidden set and ranges
setup: uv pip install -q jax==0.12.0.1 numpy==2.5.4 scipy==1.18.1
notes: Rerun of r6-dialsb-001, which its own speed guard stopped after 5 minutes (exit 3, $0.04 billed): job.sh exports OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 before it calls nproc, and GNU nproc then answers 1, so the job planned one process at a time on a 16-vCPU machine. The presmoke itself passed on the machine (every stage at full shapes, 248 s, 672 member-ticks/s per process once compiled). Only change: the environment variable S0_NPROC=16 (the machine's sysinfo shows 16 vCPUs, 62 GB); the code is the same tested commit, pinned by ref. With 16 processes the guard projects about 2,100 s. CPU ONLY, no GPU is used (jax CPU wheel, JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu). The one planned job of study dialsB (total cap of the study $5): stage 0 of the membrane carrier, the CPU gate of study B of round6/dials/PLAN.md. Rules, sizes and thresholds are in round6/dials/dialsB/DECLARED.md, committed (9c00a2d29) before any run. PILOT_NEVER_REUSE_AS_EXAM: public seeds, pilot hidden values written to $OUT, never an exam; no secret anywhere. Work (job.sh, one script, phases run 16 processes at a time, one core each): (1) presmoke: every stage once at full array shapes with short counts (one process, about 9 minutes here; exit 2 on failure); (2) speed guard: exit 3 unless the measured compiled rate projects the whole job inside 9,000 s; (3) scans: 53 points of the public law (8 members) and 13 points of the hidden carrier (16 members) in 14 processes, plus a non-fatal alignment check on the designer's pilot seed 5; (4) ranges.json by the declared rule, its SHA-256 printed before the gate starts; (5) the gate: 8 seeds x 2 arms = 16 processes of about 324,000 member-ticks each at 64 px (start states, 16 Lab episodes, 32 test items x 6 truths, the designer's gains, the adversary's command filter on its 39-point grid, a told-form fit on 72 quasi-random points, a history-only ridge stand-in); (6) analysis.json with the verdict. About 5.9 million member-ticks in all; measured here 430 member-ticks/s per process once compiled, so 3.8 CPU-hours, expected 40-70 minutes on 16 vCPUs. job.sh's own deadline is 10,800 s (S0_LIMIT_S), max_hours 3.5. Memory: 64-px fields, batches of 48 members through jax.lax.map (one member at a time), largest array 8 million elements (guard at 2^31 in Sim.roll); 16 processes, each a few GB at most while compiling. $OUT: JSON, small npz and logs, under 5 MB. No network or subprocess use outside setup except xargs/sh/timeout in job.sh. Cap: $0.54/h x (3.5 + 0.25) h = $2.03, + $0.10 = $2.13; $2.50 leaves room for a listed rate up to $0.64/h. CPU test: job.sh end to end at tiny size (S0_SIZE=tiny, smoke seeds 91, 92, one process at a time) from a git archive of exactly these five paths at commit 52ae6e403631: exit 0, 753 s; the alignment check at full size reproduces the designer's L(pub), L(pub0), L(O) on his seed 5 exactly (max difference 0.0) and picks the adversary's filter (0.25, 1, 3, 2). At tiny size the alignment step stops by design (4 members leave one test state on seed 5) and is not fatal.
